chunks: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Sakari said:

When Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid al-Qummi came on behalf of his father and the community to Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi and asked him about the matter in which it was narrated that he had claimed deputyship, he denied it and said: 'I do not have any such position from this.' Wealth was offered to him, but he refused, saying: 'It is forbidden for me to take anything from him, for I do not have any such position in this matter, nor did I claim anything from it.' And I was present when he was addressed by him in Basra.

key_terms.أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْبَغْدَادِيُّ: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, a prominent early Shia scholar and narrator.
key_terms.ابْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْو: Ibn al-Hasan al-Qummi, the individual whose claim of deputyship is being discussed.
key_terms.النِّيَابَةِ: Deputyship or representation, specifically referring to the claim of being a deputy of the Imam.
key_terms.مُحَرَّمٌ: Forbidden or prohibited, used here to emphasize the refusal of wealth based on lack of claim.

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn al-Hasan al-Qummi say about his claim of deputyship when questioned by Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the rigorous scrutiny of early claimants to the Imam’s deputyship, specifically Ibn al-Hasan al-Qummi, who denied possessing any unique authority or 'Amr' (matter) distinct from the general populace. His refusal of offered wealth underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing genuine, humble representatives from those seeking material gain or political leverage during the Minor and Major Ghayba periods. The account serves as a critical historical record for validating the authenticity of deputyship claims against potential impostors.
